title: What are currently the biggest, most polished games made largely with AI?
author: Lucko_Coldwolf
selftext:
I'm talking games with substantial content, like campaign, story content, 3d worlds, mechanics.  
Remakes, recomps, mods, and such don't count. Only "original" work.

comments.author: niloony
comments.body: There's a bunch of unreleased ones in the strategy genre that look promising like Ebbtide, Warfront, Defilade and a huge number of Total War clones. But the tools haven't been good for long enough for serious launches. You can't rush playtesting and polish and I've already seen a few delay because they realised it's still a mountain to climb. I assume Early Access is going to get a lot of games that launched too soon.

replies.author: beta_1457
replies.body: This is something that's really overlooked. There are a lot of people putting out effectively tech demos. Putting out a polished product with AI assistance, is still time consuming and balancing is one of the biggest challenges with games. They need to have the appropriate challenge/difficulty and fairness that isn't easy for AI to do (except for maybe an incremental game because those formulas can be pretty easily replicated)

comments.body: The bigger scope ones are probably still in development. From small scope, openly AI and the most successful ones, Slotbound for example, 200k+ copies.

comments.author: TheBunkers2108
comments.body: The irony is that we're all part of the same loop. We use AI to create our games, push its limits, refine workflows, and help advance the very technology that could eventually allow the companies behind it to generate entire video games from just a few prompts. In a way, we're helping build our own future competition.

comments.author: Brilliant_Feed4158
comments.body:
Well, I am biased, but I have to say my game Potato Poker is far from a "single prompt". I've been building and reiterating for two months to build the exact game I wanted to play myself.

What helps is that I have designed games before and hired a developer to build a different game. So I knew how I wanted to work with AI. In the end one can also ask AI to guide the designer through the process of writing a blueprint and workflow.
